name: RTFKT phishing campaign
rootCause: In late 2022, phishing operators impersonated RTFKT NFT campaigns and airdrops on Ethereum, including fake mint pages tied to well known RTFKT branding. Victims who signed malicious approval transactions granted attackers permission to transfer NFTs and tokens from their wallets. Public evidence does not establish a smart contract vulnerability in RTFKT or a verified aggregate loss figure. The incident involved phishing websites and fraudulent wallet approval requests. Victims signed ERC-721 setApprovalForAll or ERC-20 approval transactions that authorized attacker-controlled addresses to transfer assets from their wallets. No on-chain vulnerability in…
